hypothesis: Heavy calls are dominated by 10k MDBX B-tree seeks (node_search/cmp_lexical ~19%). A 16KB page holds 4x the keys of the default 4KB page, so the HashedStorages tree is shallower. The datadir is recreated from genesis each run, so the creation-time page size can vary per experiment.
llm_commentary: A 16KB MDBX page size (vs the default 4KB, set at genesis creation through --db.page-size) is neutral on every family against the same-boot champion: c8a 4.76→4.67s (ranges 4.67-4.84 vs 4.64-4.69 overlap), c8i 5.50→5.50s, c8g 6.84→6.79s, m9g 4.59→4.54s (inside its ~±3% drift). With only ~10k storage entries, the HashedStorages tree is a few levels deep at either page size, so the per-SLOAD cost is dominated by the key comparison work inside pages and by cursor/transaction overhead, not by tree depth. Page size could matter on a mainnet-sized database, which this benchmark does not model.
